outcome: Youssef Lazar's preprint claiming to prove the Littlewood conjecture for a restricted class of badly-approximable pairs (arXiv:2202.01596) was revised on 19 April 2025 with an 'improved main result', but the paper remains an unrefereed preprint with no citations, no journal record, and no expert digestion found; several other genuine advances in the surrounding area (Fregoli-Kleinbock on higher-dimensional obstructions, a new numerical upper-bound algorithm, a disproof of the distinct 'uniform Littlewood conjecture') either predate the window, are about related/variant problems rather than the stated conjecture, or are non-AI computational results.
summary: The triage flagged Youssef Lazar's arXiv:2202.01596, 'The Littlewood conjecture for a restricted class of pairs of real numbers,' which claims to prove the conjecture for a restricted class of badly-approximable pairs (alpha, beta) via localization of roots of a cubic equation depending on continued-fraction properties of the pair. This is a genuine case of the stated 2D conjecture (a restriction, not a variant), so it is in scope under §3.1. The paper was originally submitted 3 February 2022 (before the window) and revised 19 April 2025 (inside the window); arXiv's revision comment describes the change as 'minor changes' with an 'improved main result,' and a WebFetch read of the full text found no version-diff changelog beyond that comment. I could not confirm precisely how much new mathematical content the v2 revision contains versus the pre-window v1, but since the revision date itself falls inside the window and the comment indicates the main result was strengthened, I date the event to the v2 posting per §6.3's 'first public written argument' rule and classify status as claimed rather than open_stale, with medium confidence given the ambiguity the triage also flagged. No expert digestion, citation, or journal acceptance was found (a targeted search for citations of Lazar's paper returned nothing), so resolved is not warranted; the paper is a solo, unrefereed preprint. No AI involvement of any kind was found in this or the paper's methodology (classical continued-fraction/cubic-equation number theory). I also examined the wider 2024-2026 literature on the Littlewood conjecture: Chow-Yang's 'two-logarithm strengthening' (Inventiones 2024) traces to arXiv:1902.06081 v2 posted 2 December 2023, before the window, so it does not count as a window event. Chow-Technau's 'Dispersion and Littlewood's conjecture' was posted 27 July 2023, also pre-window. Fregoli-Kleinbock's generalization of Badziahin's logarithmic obstruction to higher-dimensional vectors (arXiv:2211.04523) reached its substantive v3 on 17 January 2024 (still pre-window) with only a notational v4 in April 2025, and in any case concerns a different, higher-dimensional problem (vectors in R^d, not pairs in R^2), so it is a related problem rather than a case of the stated conjecture. Schleischitz's 'Disproof of the uniform Littlewood conjecture' (arXiv:2603.12611, March 2026) is explicitly about a distinct, stronger 'uniform' variant (using limsup over all q up to Q rather than liminf), not the classical conjecture stated in the bullet, so it is out of scope per §3.1's variant/case distinction. Matala-Aho, Törmä and Vapa's 'Numerical Upper Bounds in the Littlewood Conjecture' (Experimental Mathematics, online 2 April 2026, received 8 April 2024) introduces a continued-fraction-based algorithm to refine numerical universal upper-bound estimates; this is classical computational number theory (not AI), and per §3.1's rule that an existence/infinitude-type question is not advanced by a tightened search bound, it would at most be 'progress' with ai_role none — it does not change the status verdict here because the Lazar claim already establishes 'claimed' as the governing status. No AI system was found credited anywhere in the current Littlewood conjecture literature.
competing_reading: If the April 2025 Lazar revision is purely a resubmission of the 2022 result with cosmetic wording changes and no new mathematical content, the correct status would be open_stale (dated to February 2022, before the frozen revision), since nothing would have actually happened inside the window. The arXiv comment 'minor changes, improved main result' is genuinely ambiguous between these two readings, and I could not obtain a clean diff between v1 and v2 to settle it.
what_would_settle_it: A diff between arXiv:2202.01596 v1 and v2 (or the author's own account of what changed) showing whether the 'improved main result' extends the restricted class of pairs covered or otherwise strengthens the mathematical content, versus being purely expository; alternatively, any expert citation or referee report engaging with the 2025 version specifically.

corrections.why: The claim is not credible enough to be the event the status rests on. A solo preprint first posted in 2022, before the window, with no citation, journal record or expert engagement in over four years, re-dated into the window only by a v2 whose own comment reads 'minor changes', is at best a pre-snapshot claim (which `open` already covers) and at worst no event at all; the record's competing_reading concedes it may be purely a resubmission. The 'restricted class of badly-approximable pairs' is also unspecified in the record, so even taken at face value it is not shown to be a non-trivial case. Everything else the record examined is either pre-window (Chow-Yang, Chow-Technau, Fregoli-Kleinbock v3), a variant (Schleischitz on the uniform conjecture), or by the record's own reading does not advance the stated question (Matala-Aho-Torma-Vapa numerical bounds). DEPARTURE FROM THE INSTRUCTIONS, STATED PLAINLY: DEEP_DIVE.md 6.1 codes any undigested preprint `claimed` and the agent followed that correctly. This correction applies a stricter rule: a claim with no expert uptake, from outside or at the margin of the field, is set aside like a withdrawn claim, and the furthest genuine event that remains sets the status. The claim stays in `outcome`, `event` and `summary` as evidence.
